name: Doh-Jamyrdoh
ingredients: 500g pork belly or shoulder, cut into cubes
1 cup fresh Jamyrdoh leaves (Houttuynia cordata), finely chopped
2 tablespoons perilla seeds (shynrai), toasted and ground
instructions: 1. Heat a heavy-bottomed pot and add the pork pieces, cooking until they release their fat and turn light brown.
2. Add the chopped onions, ginger paste, and garlic paste; sauté until the onions turn translucent.
3. Add the green chilies and salt, stirring well to coat the meat.
4. Pour in enough water to cover the meat, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer until the pork is tender.
5. Stir in the ground perilla seeds (shynrai) to thicken the gravy and add a nutty aroma.
6. Finally, fold in the fresh chopped Jamyrdoh leaves and simmer for 2-3 minutes until wilted.
7. Serve hot with steamed red rice (Jhur).
description: Doh-Jamyrdoh is a quintessential dish of the Khasi community in Meghalaya. It highlights the local reliance on foraged greens like Jamyrdoh, which offers a distinct fishy, cilantro-like aroma that balances the richness of the pork and the earthiness of perilla seeds.
